description:
## Why

stoa-mail is currently single-user: SINGLETON_USER_ID = 1 is hardcoded in server.rs. Every authenticated session maps to the same user. This is the foundational blocker for the commercial BYOA product — without multiuser, stoa cannot be sold as a WorkMail replacement.

## Scope

Everything required to support N independent users on a single stoa-mail deployment, each with isolated mailboxes, independent JMAP accounts, per-user quotas, and SMTP delivery routing by address.

## Sub-issues

- User accounts table and provisioning CLI
- Per-user storage isolation (article numbers, overview, flags, state, mailboxes)
- JMAP session endpoint returns per-user account (removes SINGLETON_USER_ID)
- JMAP request routing validates accountId ownership
- SMTP delivery routes to correct user mailbox by address
- Per-user quota enforcement
- Admin HTTP API for user management

## Definition of done

- N users can authenticate independently and see only their own mail
- SINGLETON_USER_ID is removed from the codebase
- SMTP delivery to user@domain routes to the correct mailbox
- Per-user quotas are enforced at ingest
- A provisioning CLI (stoa-mail user add/remove/list) exists
- All existing tests pass with no regressions
design: User ID (i64) is the stable internal identifier. JMAP account_id = u_{username}. Admin user flag in the users table gates the admin API. Quotas stored per user in the users table.
title: EPIC: Multi-user support
